parameters.name: table
parameters.description: The set of items to rank against. Use ALL(Table) to rank against every item, ignoring visual filters.
parameters.examNote: Without ALL(), ranks are relative to the currently visible rows only — not all items in the model.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: The value used to determine ranking order. Evaluated for each row of the table.
parameters.examNote: Must be the same measure or expression you are ranking by — a mismatch causes all items to tie at rank 1.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value to look up in the ranking. If omitted, uses the expression in the current filter context.
parameters.examNote: Almost always omitted — DAX automatically uses the current row/context as the lookup value.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: DESC (default) gives rank 1 to the highest value. ASC gives rank 1 to the lowest.
parameters.examNote: Default is DESC — rank 1 = best/highest. Specify ASC to rank smallest first (e.g., lowest cost).

parameters.name: ties
parameters.description: SKIP (default) leaves rank gaps for ties (1, 1, 3). DENSE produces consecutive ranks (1, 1, 2).
parameters.examNote: Default SKIP matches Excel RANK behavior. Use DENSE when gaps in ranking would confuse report users.

summary: RANKX returns the rank of a value within a set of values. Used to create Top N visuals, leaderboards, and product/customer rankings. The table argument controls what you rank against.

examples.label: Rank all products by total sales
examples.explanation: ALL(Products) makes every product available for comparison. RANKX evaluates SUM(Sales[Amount]) for each product. Highest sales = Rank 1 (default DESC order).

commonTraps: Without ALL(), RANKX ranks within the currently visible set. If a visual shows 5 products filtered by category, ranks go 1–5 even though there are 100 products in the model.
The expression must exactly match the measure being ranked. If they differ, every item evaluates to the same rank.
RANKX is a measure — it cannot be used directly as a calculated column in most scenarios due to its dependence on filter context.
